visibleText: A duchy of masks and bells beneath a violet eclipse. Its ruler is the Veiled Archduke, a title passed by inheritance. True names are guarded; ward-bells ring against what the eclipse lets in. Its court speaks High Korvenic; its streets, Vesper-Cant. Its Gambit is called Le Jeu des Rois Morts, the Game of Dead Kings.
A nation's sixteen are drawn from its banners. Great houses send their champions; minor houses send their levies, and levies stand in the front rank.
A pawn may become anything but a king.

A sulfur desert where an inland sea once boiled. Its Ignition Imams keep the faith and the engines alike. Its navigators see four seconds ahead; anything further is Mirage. Its tongue is Kharzani. Its Gambit is the Qimar al-Malik.

A vertical city governed by the Board. Wealth lives Cloud-side; labor lives Sump-side, where workers are entries in a ledger. The "09" is Foundry Sector 09, now sealed behind Aether fog. Its people speak Kwind-Pidgin. Its Gambit runs as Protocol K-GAMBIT.09.
An uneasy armistice signed at Vane, a spire on the borders where the four powers meet.
Painted map of Korvenia, Aethelgard, Kwind-09 and Solforiz

Seven Great Houses share a Blood-Throne, and their riders are bound to the First-Born, beasts as old as the mountains. Its people speak Old Aethel; its riders command in High Drakonic. Its Gambit is the Cyning-Slieht.
The High Sovereign's Sovereign Crown, an astral engine, tore itself apart. The calendar begins with the fall.
The four powers fought over the Crown-Shards the blast left behind.
The shards grow unstable, the truce is failing, and a generation has grown up with no memory of the old order.

When a claim cannot be settled, nations do not march armies. Each sends sixteen living representatives to the board, and the outcome decides the claim: land, passage, custody, even sovereignty. What follows the judgment is politics.
